ledger.note: About 1245: the bishop becomes a prince. The bishops 'obtained the status of Imperial immediacy about 1245'; Bishop Henry of Bilversheim became the first prince-bishop (the diocese itself dates from the 1007 synod in Frankfurt).

1631: the Swedes come. 'Bishop Johann Georg fled to his Carinthian estates in 1631.' The page does not say when Swedish troops entered Bamberg; in 1633 Bernhard of Saxe-Weimar 'obtained the title of a Duke of Franconia from the hands of the Swedish chancellor Axel Oxenstierna'.
1634: the prince-bishops 'were able to return and recover their possessions after Bernard's defeat at Nördlingen 1634'.
1759: the Carinthian estates are sold. Empress Maria Theresa 'purchased these territories in 1759': Villach, Feldkirchen, Wolfsberg, Tarvis and Kirchdorf an der Krems.

ledger.note: 1802: Bavarian troops occupy the bishopric. The last prince-bishop 'had to face the occupation by the Bavarian troops of Elector Maximilian IV Joseph in 1802'; Christoph Franz von Buseck 'officially resigned on 29 September 1802'.
25 February 1803: the Reichsdeputationshauptschluss turns the occupation into annexation: 'Bamberg was finally annexed to Bavaria'.

NOT SETTLED. (1) Start year: the page's 1245 is 'about'; the diocese is 1007 and the princely rank may be earlier. (2) Which of the Carinthian estates the bishops held before 1245 is not on the page. (3) Territorial gains and losses inside Franconia (Forchheim, Hallstadt, Kronach, Lichtenfels, Bayreuth lands) are not on the page. (4) The infobox says 'Mediatised to Bavaria in 1802', the text 1803; the dossier ends 25 February 1803 and records the 1802 Bavarian occupation. (5) The Swedish occupation start is not dated beyond the bishop's flight in 1631.
